resources.string: The host does nothing on its own. Every feature arrives as a module that runs in a sandbox and holds only the permissions you grant.
Write a script right here: pick a starting point, edit, run. No computer needed.
Permissions the module may ask for
What the code uses is switched on automatically. You still confirm permissions when the module first starts.
Letters, digits and _ . - are allowed. Nested folders: lib/net
Use Latin letters, digits and _ . - and a name that is not taken.
Full path from the module root, e.g. lib/util.lua. Changing the folders moves the file.
That path cannot be used: it is taken, invalid, or it would move a folder into itself.
The file is removed from the module when you save.
The folder and the %1$d files in it are removed from the module when you save.
Give the module a name to save and run it.
The main file %1$s of a %2$s module is empty, so there is nothing to run. Write the code in %1$s (open it in the file list), or create the module again in the language of your code.
Press Run: what the module writes appears here. A line with a file and a line number opens that place in the code.
Other files of the module, loaded from the main script with require. Folders are allowed: lib/util.%1$s
Use Latin letters, digits and _ . - with the .%1$s extension, and a name that is not taken.
A running module is restarted to pick a change up.
Leave empty to remove the value: the module will ask for it again or use its default.
A package is verified and shown for review. A script opens in the editor, where you see the code before it becomes a module.
Fingerprint of the author\'s key. Compare it with the one the author published; anyone can put any name on a package.
Installing grants nothing. Each permission is asked for separately when the module needs it.
Installed version %1$s will be replaced with %2$s. Its data and granted permissions are kept.
Starts the module when the phone boots and whenever ModuForge starts. Works only while the module is enabled and holds the background permission.
Switch on what you allow. The module starts with these; anything left off stays blocked and can be changed later on the module screen.
The question above was written by the module. Your answer goes to %1$s (%2$s) and nowhere else. Do not type passwords for unrelated accounts.
This is the key named by the install link: the package comes from the author who published the link.
The link names the author\'s key. After the download the package is checked against it and shown for review; nothing is installed before you agree.
The link does not name the author\'s key, so compare the fingerprint yourself on the next screen. Nothing is installed before you agree.
The downloaded package is signed by a different key than the link names
This install link is damaged or does not point to an https address
This module is no longer installed.
A disabled module cannot run or request permissions.
This module declares no permissions. It cannot reach the network, files, clipboard or any other resource.
A running module lives in its own isolated process. Stop asks it to finish; Kill destroys the process at once.
Disable the module to uninstall it. Its grants are removed with it.
See which apps are installed, open them and open links in them.
Take photos with the cameras of this device. Android shows its camera indicator while a photo is taken, and every photo is recorded in the audit log.

Touch the screen and read what is on it in every app: tap, swipe, type, press buttons by their text. It works through the accessibility service you turn on in the system settings, and stops when you turn it off. A notification shows while a module uses it.
Reason given by the module (not verified):
This permission lets the module act against other systems. Probing systems you do not own or have no written permission to test may be illegal.
I confirm I am authorized to test this target.
Nothing recorded yet. Every permission request, decision and module change appears here.
Lets modules that you allowed to control the screen touch it and read it. Turn it off at any time: modules lose that ability at once. ModuForge never uses it on its own.
For modules that use the camera, touch the screen or open apps. Each module needs its own permission; these switches are the system side of it.
Screen control is off: modules cannot touch or read the screen.
This edition has no screen control, so it installs on any phone. For modules that touch the screen, install the full edition (the file with “full” in its name) from the releases.
If Android refuses to turn it on because the app is restricted: open the app info of ModuForge, press ⋮ and choose Allow restricted settings.
Camera access is not allowed yet.
stopped: host left the screen and the module holds no background permission
Follow the system palette. Pick a colour below to use your own instead.
True black in the dark theme; saves power on OLED screens.
Accept modules sent from your computer with mfrg push: the module is installed and restarted without tapping through the app. Works while the app is open.
The connection point could not be opened: the port is in use. Turn the mode off and on again.
Without this only a computer connected by USB can send modules. Turn it on only in a network you trust.
Connect the phone by USB with debugging on and run in the module folder:
With the computer in the same network, run in the module folder:
The file comes from the project\'s releases on GitHub and is signed with the same key as this app. Android asks you to confirm the installation; your modules and their data are kept.
The downloaded file is not a build of this app signed with the same key, so it was not installed.
Installing is not allowed for this app yet.
Off by default: the app contacts GitHub only when you press the button. When on, it looks once at every start and tells you if there is something new.
A new version of ModuForge is available.
The host connects to the network only for modules you granted internet access, recording each connection in the audit log, and to GitHub when you check for an update or open an install link.

ModuForge is for authorized testing, learning and automation. Use modules only against systems you own or are explicitly permitted to test. Intrusive permissions require confirming authorization for each target, and every such confirmation is recorded in the audit log.
Open connections to servers on the internet. The module can send anything it has access to and download content.
Read and write files in the module\'s own isolated folder. Other modules and your files stay out of reach.
Read and write files and folders you pick outside the module\'s own storage. These may hold personal data.
Read and replace clipboard contents. The clipboard often holds passwords and other secrets.
Show notifications in the module\'s name.
Keep working while ModuForge is not on screen. This uses battery and the module acts without you watching.
Send prompts to the AI models you configured. With a cloud provider the prompts leave the device and may be billed to your API key.
Run a long-lived bot using credentials stored by the host. The bot acts under that account.
Read the device model, OS version and similar details that can identify this device.
Probe hosts on the local network. Allowed only for targets you confirm you are authorized to test.
